records.context: Only Home is rebuilt when the theme changes; every other application view is re-styled in place by re-applying the QSS. That is enough for anything whose colours come from the stylesheet, and not enough for a backdrop that paints itself — the DNA rain and the ambient background both capture their flat fill colour and their wallpaper at construction. Switching from dark to light left a black rain rectangle on a white page, and switching into Cell left it painting flat black over the micrograph the theme had just loaded. The ambient backdrop has exactly the same two captured values and therefore exactly the same two bugs.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Only Home is rebuilt when the theme changes; every other screen is re-styled in place by re-applying the QSS. That is enough for anything whose colours come from the stylesheet, and not enough for a backdrop that paints itself — the DNA rain and the ambient background both capture their flat fill colour and their wallpaper at construction. Switching from dark to light left a black rain rectangle on a white page, and switching into Cell left it painting flat black over the micrograph the theme had just loaded. The ambient backdrop has exactly the same two captured values and therefore exactly the same two bugs.
records.translation: Aðeins Home er endurbyggt þegar þemað breytist; allir aðrir skjáir eru endurstílaðir á staðnum með því að beita QSS aftur. Það dugar fyrir allt sem fær liti sína úr stílblaðinu, en ekki fyrir bakgrunn sem teiknar sig sjálfur — DNA-regnið og umhverfisbakgrunnurinn grípa bæði flatan fyllilit sinn og veggfóður við smíði. Skipti úr dökku í ljóst skildu eftir svartan regnferhyrning á hvítri síðu, og skipti yfir í Cell létu það mála flatt svart yfir smásjármyndina sem þemað hafði rétt hlaðið. Umhverfisbakgrunnurinn hefur nákvæmlega sömu tvö gripnu gildin og þar með nákvæmlega sömu tvær villurnar.

records.context: Both palette events count, and that is the whole reason this works. ``QApplication.setPalette`` — which is what :func:`spacr.qt.theme.apply_qpalette` ends in — delivers ``ApplicationPaletteChange`` **only to top-level widgets** (Qt 6.11, verified); every child, including every AppScreen inside MainWindow's stack, gets ``PaletteChange`` instead. Listening for the application event alone meant this handler fired in the tests that synthesised it and never once in the running app.

records.source: Both palette events count, and that is the whole reason this works. ``QApplication.setPalette`` — which is what :func:`spacr.qt.theme.apply_qpalette` ends in — delivers ``ApplicationPaletteChange`` **only to top-level widgets** (Qt 6.11, verified); every child, including every AppScreen inside MainWindow's stack, gets ``PaletteChange`` instead. Listening for the application event alone meant this handler fired in the tests that synthesised it and never once in the running app.
records.translation: Bæði litaspjaldsatvikin teljast með, og það er öll ástæðan fyrir því að þetta virkar. ``QApplication.setPalette`` — sem :func:`spacr.qt.theme.apply_qpalette` endar í — sendir ``ApplicationPaletteChange`` **aðeins til efstu græja** (Qt 6.11, staðfest); hver undirgræja, þar á meðal hver AppScreen í staflanum í MainWindow, fær ``PaletteChange`` í staðinn. Ef aðeins var hlustað eftir forritsatvikinu var þessi meðhöndlari kallaður í prófunum sem bjuggu það til en aldrei í keyrandi forritinu.

records.context: Every module application view **except** the ones that already animate something of their own — which today is exactly :data:`DNA_RAIN_APPS`. Sequencing's rain is *about* sequencing: bases falling behind the application view that maps reads to barcodes. Putting a second, unrelated animation behind it would fight it — two independent motions competing for the same pixels, neither readable, and two animation timers executing on the one application view that already had one. So an application view gets one animated background or none, never both.

Putting a second, unrelated animation behind it would fight it — two independent motions competing for the same pixels, neither readable, and two animation timers running on the one screen that already had one. So a screen gets one animated background or none, never both.
records.translation: Hver einingaskjár **nema** þeir sem þegar hreyfa eitthvað eigið — sem í dag eru nákvæmlega :data:`DNA_RAIN_APPS`. Regn raðgreiningarinnar *fjallar um* raðgreiningu: basar sem falla á bak við skjáinn sem varpar lestrum á strikamerki. Að setja aðra, óskylda hreyfimynd á bak við það myndi togast á við það — tvær óháðar hreyfingar sem keppa um sömu pixla, hvorug læsileg, og tveir hreyfimyndatímar á þeim eina skjá sem þegar hafði einn. records.context: The run uses a worker. **Execution model:** completion returns to the GUI thread. ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted *inside the worker thread*; therefore each receiver that changes a widget uses an explicit queued connection to a bound method of this GUI-thread widget.

records.source: **The run happens off the GUI thread, and its completion handler comes back onto it.** ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted *in the worker thread*; every widget-mutating receiver therefore uses an explicit queued connection to a bound method of this GUI-thread widget.

records.context: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks, and the analysis assumes that the controls behave the same way every time. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all measure against them, so when the controls drift, every downstream result shifts with them without any warning — the analysis normalises to whatever controls it is handed.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.control_chart#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks, and the analysis assumes that the controls behave the same way every time. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all measure against them, so when the controls drift, every downstream result shifts with them without any warning — the analysis normalises to whatever controls it is handed.
records.translation: Skimunarherferð samanstendur af tugum platna sem keyrðar eru á vikum, og greiningin gerir ráð fyrir að viðmiðin hegði sér eins í hvert skipti. Val á smellum, stöðlun platna og Z' eru öll mæld miðað við þau, svo þegar viðmiðin reka færast allar niðurstöður sem á eftir koma með þeim án nokkurrar viðvörunar — greiningin staðlar við hvaða viðmið sem henni eru gefin.

records.context: Everything numeric comes from :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart`, which has no Qt in it and documents the reasoning for every decision — most of all the central one, that sigma comes from the average moving range over d2 and never from the standard deviation of the series, because the SD is inflated by exactly the drift the chart exists to detect. This file draws that result and nothing else: no statistic is computed here, so the chart on application view and the chart in a report cannot disagree.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.control_chart#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Everything numeric comes from :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart`, which has no Qt in it and documents the reasoning for every decision — most of all the central one, that sigma comes from the average moving range over d2 and never from the standard deviation of the series, because the SD is inflated by exactly the drift the chart exists to detect. This file draws that result and nothing else: no statistic is computed here, so the chart on screen and the chart in a report cannot disagree.
records.translation: Allt tölulegt kemur úr :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart`, sem inniheldur ekkert Qt og skjalfestir rökin fyrir hverri ákvörðun — einkum þeirri meginákvörðun að sigma komi úr meðalhreyfispönn deilt með d2 og aldrei úr staðalfráviki raðarinnar, því SD er uppblásið af nákvæmlega því reki sem ritið er til að greina. Þessi skrá teiknar þá niðurstöðu og ekkert annað: engin tölfræði er reiknuð hér, svo ritið á skjánum og ritið í skýrslu geta ekki stangast á.

records.source: It shows the total, the item list and every file that would go — the same list :meth:`spacr.data_manager.PrunePlan.file_list` returns, not a summary of it — and its accept button stays disabled until the user ticks the box that says they have read it. The box is not pre-ticked and is not a plain OK, because the deletion cannot be undone.
records.translation: Hann sýnir heildina, atriðalistann og hverja skrá sem myndi hverfa — sama lista og :meth:`spacr.data_manager.PrunePlan.file_list` skilar, ekki samantekt á honum — og samþykkishnappur hans helst óvirkur þar til notandinn hakar í reitinn sem segir að hann hafi lesið hann. Reiturinn er ekki forhakaður og er ekki einfalt OK, því ekki er hægt að afturkalla eyðinguna.

records.context: The dialog fills in two stages. The file list is not stored on the plan: every call to ``file_list`` runs ``os.walk`` over every candidate directory, because a plan for a project with millions of extracted image regions must not carry millions of strings. Doing that in ``__init__`` would put a full recursive walk of the user's project on the main GUI execution path, at the one moment they are waiting for a window to appear — and on a share that is asleep, the walk's first stat alone can take twenty seconds while the mount wakes. So the dialog opens with the half that needs nothing from the disk (the totals, every candidate, every kept item and its reason) and the file list arrives behind it. Nothing is dropped: the user still reads every path before anything is deleted, which is why the acknowledgement is held disabled until the list is on application view — or, when the walk fails, until :meth:`_on_listing_failed` has said so in the list's place. The box is never enabled while the list shows a placeholder.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.data_manager.ConfirmDeleteDialog#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The dialog fills in two stages. The file list is not stored on the plan: every call to ``file_list`` runs ``os.walk`` over every candidate directory, because a plan for a project with millions of crops must not carry millions of strings. Doing that in ``__init__`` would put a full recursive walk of the user's project on the GUI thread, at the one moment they are waiting for a window to appear — and on a share that is asleep, the walk's first stat alone can take twenty seconds while the mount wakes. So the dialog opens with the half that needs nothing from the disk (the totals, every candidate, every kept item and its reason) and the file list arrives behind it. Nothing is dropped: the user still reads every path before anything is deleted, which is why the acknowledgement is held disabled until the list is on screen — or, when the walk fails, until :meth:`_on_listing_failed` has said so in the list's place. The box is never enabled while the list shows a placeholder.
records.translation: Glugginn fyllist í tveimur áföngum. Skráalistinn er ekki geymdur í áætluninni: hvert kall á ``file_list`` keyrir ``os.walk`` yfir hverja kandídatsmöppu, því áætlun fyrir verkefni með milljónir myndskurða má ekki bera milljónir strengja. Að gera það í ``__init__`` myndi setja fulla endurkvæma göngu um verkefni notandans á GUI-þráðinn, einmitt á því augnabliki sem hann bíður eftir að gluggi birtist — og á sameign sem er í dvala getur fyrsta stat-kall göngunnar eitt og sér tekið tuttugu sekúndur á meðan tengingin vaknar. Því opnast glugginn með þeim helmingi sem þarf ekkert af diskinum (heildirnar, hvern kandídat, hvert haldið atriði og ástæðu þess) og skráalistinn kemur á eftir. Engu er sleppt: notandinn les samt hverja slóð áður en nokkru er eytt, og þess vegna er staðfestingunni haldið óvirkri þar til listinn er á skjánum — eða, þegar gangan mistekst, þar til :meth:`_on_listing_failed` hefur sagt frá því í stað listans. Reiturinn er aldrei virkur á meðan listinn sýnir staðgengil.

records.translation: **Breytingar eru tafarlausar og staðbundnar.** Breyting á reit kallar á :meth:`spacr.foreign.ImportPlan.with_column_maps`, sem leysir dálkana upp á nýtt án þess að snerta diskinn, svo listinn yfir óvarpaða dálka, árekstralistinn og Import-hnappurinn uppfærast á meðan þú skrifar.

records.context: **Off the main GUI execution path.** Scanning a plate of TIFFs and reading every label image takes seconds; the import takes minutes. Both go through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, and the completion handler is reached through a *bound method* (:attr:`ForeignScreen._job_settled`) rather than a closure, because ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted in the background execution unit and a closure connected to it would build widget children there. Tests pass ``threaded=False``.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.foreign#6

records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Scanning a plate of TIFFs and reading every label image takes seconds; the import takes minutes. Both go through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, and the completion handler is reached through a *bound method* (:attr:`ForeignScreen._job_settled`) rather than a closure, because ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted in the worker thread and a closure connected to it would build widget children there. Tests pass ``threaded=False``.
records.translation: **Utan GUI-þráðarins.** Skönnun plötu af TIFFs og lestur hverrar merkjamyndar tekur sekúndur; innflutningurinn tekur mínútur. records.context: Nothing here touches the file on the main GUI execution path. The read executes on a background execution unit -- ``SELECT * FROM cell`` into pandas measures 1.5 s for a 200 000-row measurement table on a warm local SSD -- and listing the tables runs there too, even though one ``sqlite_master`` query costs 0.4 ms, because that cost holds only for a disk that answers. Measured on one workstation, a single ``stat`` under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- had not returned after twenty seconds, and ``sqlite3.connect`` opens the file before it can read a byte of ``sqlite_master``. Picking a measurements.db off a sleeping share, or dropping a project folder that resolves onto one, would freeze the whole window with no traceback.

records.source: Nothing here touches the file on the GUI thread. The read runs on a worker thread -- ``SELECT * FROM cell`` into pandas measures 1.5 s for a 200 000-row measurement table on a warm local SSD -- and listing the tables runs there too, even though one ``sqlite_master`` query costs 0.4 ms, because that cost holds only for a disk that answers. Measured on one workstation, a single ``stat`` under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- had not returned after twenty seconds, and ``sqlite3.connect`` opens the file before it can read a byte of ``sqlite_master``. Picking a measurements.db off a sleeping share, or dropping a project folder that resolves onto one, would freeze the whole window with no traceback.

Mælt á einni vinnustöð: eitt ``stat`` undir ``/nas_mnt`` -- ``autofs``-tenging þar sem sameignin var í dvala -- hafði ekki skilað eftir tuttugu sekúndur, og ``sqlite3.connect`` opnar skrána áður en það getur lesið eitt bæti af ``sqlite_master``. records.source: **Scan writes nothing.** :func:`spacr.image_import.plan_import` walks a sample of the tree and reads each file's own axis metadata; ``Import`` is a separate press, and it stays disabled while the plan has a problem — because every problem the plan states is a way for the result to be quietly wrong, and the import is the irreversible half.
records.translation: **Skönnun skrifar ekkert.** :func:`spacr.image_import.plan_import` gengur um úrtak af trénu og les eigin ásalýsigögn hverrar skrár; ``Import`` er sérstök ýting, og hún helst óvirk á meðan áætlunin hefur vandamál — því hvert vandamál sem áætlunin tilgreinir er leið til að niðurstaðan verði hljóðlaust röng, og innflutningurinn er óafturkræfi helmingurinn.

records.context: **The proposal table is not editable, and the answer table is.** A wrong guess is never wrong for one file: it is wrong for a token position, in every name that has one. So the correction is made where the mistake lives, one answer fixing every file that shares it, rather than by retyping eight thousand rows. That is also the only correction :meth:`spacr.image_import.ImportPlan.with_mapping` can apply without re-walking the disk, which is what makes editing instant.

records.source: **The proposal table is not editable, and the answer table is.** A wrong guess is never wrong for one file: it is wrong for a token position, in every name that has one. That is also the only correction :meth:`spacr.image_import.ImportPlan.with_mapping` can apply without re-walking the disk, which is what makes editing instant.
records.translation: **Tillögutöflunni er ekki hægt að breyta, en svaratöflunni er það.** Röng ágiskun er aldrei röng fyrir eina skrá: hún er röng fyrir stöðu tóka, í hverju heiti sem hefur slíkan. Því er leiðréttingin gerð þar sem mistökin búa, eitt svar sem lagar hverja skrá sem deilir því, frekar en með því að slá inn átta þúsund línur aftur. Það er líka eina leiðréttingin sem :meth:`spacr.image_import.ImportPlan.with_mapping` getur beitt án þess að ganga aftur um diskinn, sem er það sem gerir breytingar tafarlausar.

records.context: **Off the main GUI execution path.** A scan reads every file's header; an import of a 400-plate archive takes minutes. Both go through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, and the completion handler is reached through a *bound method* (:attr:`ImageImportScreen._job_settled`) rather than a closure, because ``PipelineWorker.finished`` is emitted in the background execution unit and a closure connected to it would build widget children there. Tests pass ``threaded=False``.

records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** A scan reads every file's header; an import of a 400-plate archive takes minutes. Tests pass ``threaded=False``.
records.translation: **Utan GUI-þráðarins.** Skönnun les haus hverrar skrár; innflutningur 400 platna safns tekur mínútur. Hvort tveggja fer í gegnum :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, og lokameðhöndlaranum er náð í gegnum *bundna aðferð* (:attr:`ImageImportScreen._job_settled`) frekar en lokun, því ``PipelineWorker.finished`` er sent á vinnuþræðinum og lokun sem tengd er við það myndi byggja barnagræjur þar. Prófanir senda ``threaded=False``.

records.context: What is on application view, and why each part is there. The findings table carries the observed rate and the rate expected by coincidence in adjacent columns, with the ratio between them beside both, because a rate alone cannot be told from an accident and this panel exists to stop somebody acting on one. The text window shows reads with their matches coloured by barcode type, because a barcode landing in the same columns on row after row is the evidence that settles an argument a percentage cannot. The proposal shows the value the form holds beside the value the search suggests, so what Apply is about to do is legible before it does it.

records.context: The hook is ``done``, not ``reject`` and not ``closeEvent`` alone. records.source: The hook is ``done``, not ``reject`` and not ``closeEvent`` alone. Overriding ``reject`` to close instead would loop: ``QDialog.closeEvent`` itself calls ``reject``.
records.translation: Krókurinn er ``done``, ekki ``reject`` og ekki ``closeEvent`` eitt og sér. Ef ``reject`` væri yfirskrifað til að loka í staðinn myndi það lykkjast: ``QDialog.closeEvent`` kallar sjálft á ``reject``.

records.context: **The model never sees the data.** It sees the digest — numbers already computed — and writes prose around them. Then every number it wrote is checked back against the digest, and a draft carrying a figure that is not there is refused: the panel says which numbers were invented, keeps the model's text where you can read it, and shows the sections spaCR wrote from the digest instead. The result of the check is shown in the strip under the tabs.

records.source: **The model never sees the data.** It sees the digest — numbers already computed — and writes prose around them. Then every number it wrote is checked back against the digest, and a draft carrying a figure that is not there is refused: the panel says which numbers were invented, keeps the model's text where you can read it, and shows the sections spaCR wrote from the digest instead. The result of the check is shown in the strip under the tabs.
records.translation: **Líkanið sér aldrei gögnin.** Það sér samantektina — tölur sem þegar hafa verið reiknaðar — og skrifar texta utan um þær. Síðan er hver tala sem það skrifaði borin aftur saman við samantektina, og drögum sem bera tölu sem ekki er þar er hafnað: spjaldið segir hvaða tölur voru uppdiktaðar, heldur texta líkansins þar sem þú getur lesið hann og sýnir í staðinn kaflana sem spaCR skrifaði út frá samantektinni. Niðurstaða athugunarinnar er sýnd í ræmunni undir flipunum.

records.context: **The resolved-parameter table.** Cellpose 4 accepts ``model_type``, ``diam_mean``, ``nchan``, ``channels`` and ``rescale`` and then ignores every one of them, and it resolves all the pre-SAM model names to ``cpsam``. records.source: **The resolved-parameter table.** Cellpose 4 accepts ``model_type``, ``diam_mean``, ``nchan``, ``channels`` and ``rescale`` and then ignores every one of them, and it resolves all the pre-SAM model names to ``cpsam``. A comparison that differs only in one of those reports "no difference", which reads as "the models are equivalent" rather than "you changed nothing". So the screen shows what actually reached each model, marks what was dropped, and says so in a banner above the numbers.
records.translation: **Tafla uppleystra færibreyta.** Cellpose 4 tekur við ``model_type``, ``diam_mean``, ``nchan``, ``channels`` og ``rescale`` og hunsar síðan hverja og eina, og það leysir öll líkanaheiti frá því fyrir SAM upp í ``cpsam``. Samanburður sem er aðeins ólíkur í einni þeirra tilkynnir "no difference" (enginn munur), sem er lesið sem "the models are equivalent" (líkönin jafngild) frekar en "you changed nothing" (þú breyttir engu). Því sýnir skjárinn hvað raunverulega barst hverju líkani, merkir það sem var fellt út og segir frá því í borða fyrir ofan tölurnar.

records.context: A filter change **recomputes** the decomposition rather than just re-drawing it. PCA is a property of a population: the centre, the scale and the component directions are all computed from the rows in it. Keeping the old components and dropping the filtered points would draw a plot whose axes belong to a population the user is no longer looking at — the scores would still be in the old basis, and a cluster that separates in the filtered subset would not appear. So the filter is upstream of the maths, the recomputation is debounced, and the report under the plot re-states the row count every time.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.pca#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A filter change **recomputes** the decomposition rather than just re-drawing it. PCA is a property of a population: the centre, the scale and the component directions are all computed from the rows in it. Keeping the old components and dropping the filtered points would draw a plot whose axes belong to a population the user is no longer looking at — the scores would still be in the old basis, and a cluster that separates in the filtered subset would not appear. So the filter is upstream of the maths, the recomputation is debounced, and the report under the plot re-states the row count every time.
records.translation: Breyting á síu **endurreiknar** þáttunina frekar en að teikna hana aðeins aftur. PCA er eiginleiki þýðis: miðjan, kvarðinn og stefnur þáttanna eru öll reiknuð út frá línunum í því. Að halda gömlu þáttunum og sleppa síuðu punktunum myndi teikna graf þar sem ásarnir tilheyra þýði sem notandinn er ekki lengur að skoða — stigin væru enn í gamla grunninum, og klasi sem skilst að í síaða hlutmenginu myndi ekki birtast. Því er sían á undan stærðfræðinni, endurreikningnum er seinkað og skýrslan undir grafinu tilgreinir línufjöldann í hvert sinn.

records.source: The aggregation runs off the GUI thread. ``pqc.plate_layout`` is a full-frame groupby and ``detect_edge_effect`` a second pass over the result: **487 ms** on a real measurement table, measured, and it fired on every tick of the min-objects spin box. Dragging that box was a sequence of half-second freezes.
records.translation: Samantektin keyrir utan GUI-þráðarins. ``pqc.plate_layout`` er groupby yfir allan rammann og ``detect_edge_effect`` önnur umferð yfir niðurstöðuna: **487 ms** á raunverulegri mælingatöflu, mælt, og þetta fór af stað við hvert tif í snúningsreitnum fyrir lágmarksfjölda hluta. Að draga þann reit var röð hálfrar sekúndu frystinga.

records.context: ``recompute()`` returns a bool that a caller reads, and it means "a plate was drawn **or is being drawn**" rather than "a plate was drawn". The refusals -- no frame yet, and a failed aggregation -- are unchanged and still synchronous, because the first does no work and the second is reported by the completion handler in exactly the place it was reported before. So the only caller-visible difference is that ``True`` may arrive before the grid is painted.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.plate_view.PlateViewScreen.recompute#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``recompute()`` returns a bool that a caller reads, and it means "a plate was drawn **or is being drawn**" rather than "a plate was drawn". The refusals -- no frame yet, and a failed aggregation -- are unchanged and still synchronous, because the first does no work and the second is reported by the completion handler in exactly the place it was reported before. So the only caller-visible difference is that ``True`` may arrive before the grid is painted.
records.translation: ``recompute()`` skilar bool-gildi sem kallandi les, og það merkir „plata var teiknuð **eða er í teikningu**“ frekar en "a plate was drawn" (plata var teiknuð). Höfnunin -- enginn rammi enn, og misheppnuð samantekt -- er óbreytt og enn samstillt, því sú fyrri vinnur enga vinnu og sú seinni er tilkynnt af lokameðhöndlaranum á nákvæmlega þeim stað sem hún var tilkynnt áður. Því er eini munurinn sem kallandi sér að ``True`` getur borist áður en hnitanetið er málað.

records.context: ``_QueueRunner`` is parented to this widget and executes whole workflows, so its independent execution path can be hours long. Destroying the application view with it executing deletes a live QThread, which Qt answers with ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")``. It also does not go through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, so the process-wide run registry — and therefore ``MainWindow.closeEvent``'s drain — cannot see it.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.queue.QueueScreen.closeEvent#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``_QueueRunner`` is parented to this widget and executes whole pipelines, so its thread can be hours long. Destroying the screen with it running deletes a live QThread, which Qt answers with ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")``. It also does not go through :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, so the process-wide run registry — and therefore ``MainWindow.closeEvent``'s drain — cannot see it.
records.translation: ``_QueueRunner`` hefur þessa græju sem foreldri og keyrir heil vinnsluferli, svo þráður hans getur staðið í klukkustundir. Að eyða skjánum á meðan hann keyrir eyðir lifandi QThread, sem Qt svarar með ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")``. Hann fer heldur ekki í gegnum :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, svo keyrsluskrá alls ferlisins — og þar með tæming ``MainWindow.closeEvent`` — getur ekki séð hann.

records.context: **Volcano Explorer** is the only publication-figure path in spaCR. Its volcano is a matplotlib render behind a 56-field style that can be saved and reloaded as JSON, every called point labelled, colour or shape driven by an annotation file merged on an inferred structured-data name, arbitrary x/y columns, and a vector re-render at journal size. The panel's own volcano is pyqtgraph and can honour none of it, so the explorer is offered from that plot's own menu as "Publication figure…", seeded with the frame already on application view.

records.source: **Volcano Explorer** is the only publication-figure path in spaCR. Its volcano is a matplotlib render behind a 56-field style that can be saved and reloaded as JSON, every called point labelled, colour or shape driven by an annotation file merged on an inferred key, arbitrary x/y columns, and a vector re-render at journal size. The panel's own volcano is pyqtgraph and can honour none of it, so the explorer is offered from that plot's own menu as "Publication figure…", seeded with the frame already on screen.
records.translation: **Volcano Explorer** er eina leiðin í spaCR að myndum til birtingar. Eldfjallarit þess er matplotlib-teikning á bak við 56 reita stíl sem hægt er að vista og hlaða aftur sem JSON, þar sem hver kallaður punktur er merktur, litur eða lögun stýrist af skýringaskrá sem sameinuð er á ályktuðum lykli, hvaða x/y-dálkar sem er, og vigurendurteikning í stærð tímarits. Eigið eldfjallarit spjaldsins er pyqtgraph og getur ekki virt neitt af þessu, svo könnuðurinn er boðinn úr eigin valmynd þess grafs sem "Publication figure…", forfylltur með rammanum sem þegar er sýnilegur.

records.context: **Hit List** displays one ranked row per gene for the loaded regression processing session. Backends that report p-values receive Benjamini–Hochberg q-values computed across the genes tested; penalised backends instead rank by bootstrap selection frequency and do not report q-values. Each row includes the effect estimate, a 95% interval when a standard error is available, and gRNA sign agreement when guide-level coefficients are available. Annotation CSVs are collapsed to one row per gene before validated many-to-one joins. The complete :class:`~spacr.qt.screens.hit_list.HitListScreen` is installed as the **Hits** tab after Guide support, follows the processing session loaded by the results panel, and exports the displayed filtered list as CSV, Markdown, or self-contained HTML.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.regression#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Hit List** displays one ranked row per gene for the loaded regression run. Backends that report p-values receive Benjamini–Hochberg q-values computed across the genes tested; penalised backends instead rank by bootstrap selection frequency and do not report q-values. Each row includes the effect estimate, a 95% interval when a standard error is available, and gRNA sign agreement when guide-level coefficients are available. Annotation CSVs are collapsed to one row per gene before validated many-to-one joins. The complete :class:`~spacr.qt.screens.hit_list.HitListScreen` is installed as the **Hits** tab after Guide support, follows the run loaded by the results panel, and exports the displayed filtered list as CSV, Markdown, or self-contained HTML.
records.translation: **Hit List** sýnir eina raðaða línu fyrir hvert gen fyrir hlaðna aðhvarfskeyrslu. Bakendar sem tilkynna p-gildi fá Benjamini–Hochberg q-gildi reiknuð yfir prófuðu genin; refsaðir bakendar raða í staðinn eftir valtíðni í bootstrap-úrtökum og tilkynna ekki q-gildi. Hver lína inniheldur áhrifamatið, 95% bil þegar staðalskekkja er tiltæk og samræmi formerkja gRNA þegar stuðlar á stigi leiðsagnarraða eru tiltækir. Skýringa-CSVs eru þjappaðar í eina línu fyrir hvert gen áður en staðfestar margir-á-móti-einum-tengingar eru gerðar. Heila :class:`~spacr.qt.screens.hit_list.HitListScreen` er sett upp sem **Hits**-flipinn á eftir Guide support, fylgir keyrslunni sem niðurstöðuspjaldið hleður og flytur birta síaða listann út sem CSV, Markdown eða sjálfstætt HTML.

records.context: Each volcano shows one correction family. A guide permutation writes every minimum-support family stacked into one long table, and fits one family per response when several outcomes were fitted. Each of those is its own Benjamini-Hochberg family, so drawing the table unfiltered puts a guide on the plot two to four times at different heights and pools two corrections into one picture. :func:`single_correction_family` is the cut, and :func:`install_correction_families` puts it in front of the panel's own ``set_frame`` so every route into the panel -- a finished processing session, a folder opened by hand, a dropped bundle -- draws one family.

records.source: Each volcano shows one correction family. A guide permutation writes every minimum-support family stacked into one long table, and fits one family per response when several outcomes were fitted. Each of those is its own Benjamini-Hochberg family, so drawing the table unfiltered puts a guide on the plot two to four times at different heights and pools two corrections into one picture. :func:`single_correction_family` is the cut, and :func:`install_correction_families` puts it in front of the panel's own ``set_frame`` so every route into the panel -- a finished run, a folder opened by hand, a dropped bundle -- draws one family.
records.translation: Hvert eldfjallarit sýnir eina leiðréttingarfjölskyldu. Umröðun leiðsagnarraða skrifar hverja fjölskyldu lágmarksstuðnings staflaða í eina langa töflu, og aðfellir eina fjölskyldu fyrir hverja svörun þegar nokkrar útkomur voru aðfelldar. Hver þeirra er eigin Benjamini-Hochberg-fjölskylda, svo ef taflan er teiknuð ósíuð birtist leiðsagnarröð á grafinu tvisvar til fjórum sinnum í mismunandi hæð og tvær leiðréttingar sameinast í einni mynd. :func:`single_correction_family` er skurðurinn, og :func:`install_correction_families` setur hann fyrir framan eigið ``set_frame`` spjaldsins svo hver leið inn í spjaldið -- lokin keyrsla, mappa sem opnuð er handvirkt, búnti sem er sleppt -- teikni eina fjölskyldu.

records.context: A guide permutation fits the same guides once per minimum-support threshold and once per response, stacks the lot into one long table, and corrects each stack separately. Two things follow, and both mislead on a plot: the same guide is drawn two to four times at different heights, and two Benjamini-Hochberg corrections share one axis -- so a q-value read off the picture belongs to whichever family the point came from, which nothing on the picture says.

records.source: A guide permutation fits the same guides once per minimum-support threshold and once per response, stacks the lot into one long table, and corrects each stack separately. Two things follow, and both mislead on a plot: the same guide is drawn two to four times at different heights, and two Benjamini-Hochberg corrections share one axis -- so a q-value read off the picture belongs to whichever family the point came from, which nothing on the picture says.
records.translation: Umröðun leiðsagnarraða aðfellir sömu leiðsagnarraðir einu sinni fyrir hvern þröskuld lágmarksstuðnings og einu sinni fyrir hverja svörun, staflar öllu í eina langa töflu og leiðréttir hvern stafla sérstaklega. Tvennt leiðir af því, og hvort tveggja villir um á grafi: sama leiðsagnarröð er teiknuð tvisvar til fjórum sinnum í mismunandi hæð, og tvær Benjamini-Hochberg-leiðréttingar deila einum ás -- svo q-gildi sem lesið er af myndinni tilheyrir þeirri fjölskyldu sem punkturinn kom úr, sem ekkert á myndinni segir.

records.context: It is also named in ``spacr.qt.app._SELF_REGISTERING_APPS`` and in :data:`spacr.qt.SELF_REGISTERING_MODULES`. records.context: When the active tab changes, settings named by the ``cellpose_masks`` propagation map in :mod:`spacr.qt.preview_registry` are copied to the destination tab when that tab exposes the corresponding setting. ``src`` and ``model_name`` are not copied. On entry to Apply, the workbench searches ``<train-src>/models/cellpose_model/models`` for checkpoints whose names begin with the Train tab's ``model_name``. It prefers completed checkpoints over periodic ``_epoch_`` checkpoints and selects the most recently modified candidate from the preferred group. If found, that path is assigned to ``custom_model``, which :func:`spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune` resolves before ``model_name``; otherwise, Apply retains its current model selection.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.train_cellpose#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: When the active tab changes, settings named by the ``cellpose_masks`` propagation map in :mod:`spacr.qt.preview_registry` are copied to the destination tab when that tab exposes the corresponding setting. ``src`` and ``model_name`` are not copied. On entry to Apply, the workbench searches ``<train-src>/models/cellpose_model/models`` for checkpoints whose names begin with the Train tab's ``model_name``. It prefers completed checkpoints over periodic ``_epoch_`` checkpoints and selects the most recently modified candidate from the preferred group. If found, that path is assigned to ``custom_model``, which :func:`spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune` resolves before ``model_name``; otherwise, Apply retains its current model selection.
records.translation: Þegar virki flipinn breytist eru stillingar sem nefndar eru í ``cellpose_masks``-dreifingarvörpuninni í :mod:`spacr.qt.preview_registry` afritaðar yfir á áfangaflipann þegar sá flipi býður upp á samsvarandi stillingu. ``src`` og ``model_name`` eru ekki afrituð. Við komu á Apply leitar vinnubekkurinn í ``<train-src>/models/cellpose_model/models`` að vistunarpunktum sem byrja á ``model_name`` Train-flipans. Hann tekur fullkláraða vistunarpunkta fram yfir reglulega ``_epoch_``-vistunarpunkta og velur þann kandídat úr forgangshópnum sem síðast var breytt. Ef hann finnst er sú slóð sett í ``custom_model``, sem :func:`spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune` leysir upp á undan ``model_name``; annars heldur Apply núverandi vali sínu á líkani.

records.context: ``FigureCanvasQT.__init__`` sets ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` and a white palette, and the figure carries a solid ``facecolor``. records.source: ``FigureCanvasQT.__init__`` sets ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` and a white palette, and the figure carries a solid ``facecolor``. Three opaque things stacked: the area right of "Runs found" was a flat dark rectangle whatever the page-opacity slider said, with square corners where every other container on the page has rounded ones.
records.translation: ``FigureCanvasQT.__init__`` stillir ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` og hvítt litaspjald, og myndin ber heilan ``facecolor``. Þrír ógegnsæir hlutir staflaðir: svæðið hægra megin við "Runs found" var flatur dökkur ferhyrningur hvað sem sleði síðugegnsæis sagði, með ferköntuð horn þar sem öll önnur ílát á síðunni hafa rúnnuð.

records.context: QSS cannot fix that — a ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` widget never lets the sheet's background through, and a stylesheet cannot round a canvas matplotlib draws edge to edge. So the panel is drawn in ``paintEvent``, underneath the figure, and the figure's own patch is made fully transparent so the panel is what shows.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.train_compare.panel_canvas_class#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: QSS cannot fix that — a ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` widget never lets the sheet's background through, and a stylesheet cannot round a canvas matplotlib draws edge to edge. So the panel is drawn in ``paintEvent``, underneath the figure, and the figure's own patch is made fully transparent so the panel is what shows.
records.translation: QSS getur ekki lagað það — græja með ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent`` hleypir aldrei bakgrunni stílblaðsins í gegn, og stílblað getur ekki rúnnað striga sem matplotlib teiknar út á brúnir. Því er spjaldið teiknað í ``paintEvent``, undir myndinni, og eigin flötur myndarinnar er gerður alveg gegnsær svo spjaldið er það sem sést.
